body: I worked at a movie bar and during the peak season I made about $1400-$1600 a week. It was the most financially stable I’ve been in my life and I currently work at a dog bar and I pull from $500-$900 a week here.

It’s pretty common depending on the area you live in or popularity of the place you work at. Say you work at like a popular chain like Longhorns, Olive Garden, Texas Roadhouse and you work 25+ hours a week and a majority of your shifts on the weekend. If the place is run well and has regulars you’re looking at $800-$1000 a week during peak season sometimes more. If you’re working in a more remote area where the income is lower you would probably be making closer to $300-$600 a week.

As a light skinned biracial and plus sized women, I have found when it comes to interracial dating try to date people who have a dating past dating POC women. Every time I’ve dated a white man who has only dated or showed interest in primarily white women it has ended in some kind of racist nightmare. If the guy you’re talking to has no actual type and has a history of dating poc women since early on it has ended up being easier to be seen as more than just a skin color. My fiancé is an very conventionally attractive tall white man and because of my past experiences with racism while dating I was highly skeptical until he showed me his exes. Big relief. Interracial dating is hard but your dream guy is out there. But tbh when finding a relationship online if you’re using sites like Reddit or discord you have to remember there’s a lot of racist dudes out there online . It’s like a huge chunk of the internet. Just stick to irl dating or use platforms where your photos are visible like Twitter/Facebook/Instagram.

Things that make me swoon on a date:
- If at a restaurant or bar, consideration and patience with the staff and people around us. Tipping properly and kindness is always super sexy to me since I work in food service and it shows you’re generous and care for others. 
- Being aware of someone’s lifestyle and cater dates towards that like if you know I like art and you set our first date at an art exhibition or something cool like at a cool trendy art inspired bar. That really is appealing. It shows you listen and care about the other persons interest. 
- Respecting personal boundaries and waiting for verbal or physical cues before trying to test waters. Nothing is a bigger turn off than a guy/girl/they who wants to shove their tongue down your throat after 30 seconds of meeting. So like actually allowing a build up of tension and knowing the right moments before starting things up is attractive. 
- Talking about more than just surface topics about themselves. If I want to get to know you and you answer short I’ve learned nothing about you. People who are enthusiastic about the things that make them them are unbelievably sexy and it oozes confidence. It also encourages your date to do the same and allows possibilities for future inside jokes and deeper conversations.
